      The right material for Sacramento's climate

      Sacramento gets about 18 inches of rain a year, on roughly 57 days, and relative humidity averages 78% in the morning and 45% in the afternoon. The weather rarely decides the material here. The room does:

      • Most restrooms (offices, restaurants, retail, clinics, schools): all five materials work. Choose on looks, cleaning routine and budget.
      • Rooms that get wet from the inside (pool facilities, gym locker rooms, restrooms that are hosed down): choose solid plastic (HDPE) or phenolic. Both are solid all the way through and handle constant moisture.

      Plastic laminate has a particleboard core that may swell with excessive moisture, and powder coated steel can rust where the coating is damaged, so keep both for dry rooms. Stainless steel resists corrosion and suits premium public restrooms. Compare all five on the partitions page.

      The rules a Sacramento restroom has to meet

      • Wheelchair access: a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and California's own access rules both set the sizes, and California's are stricter in places. A remodel can also oblige you to bring the restrooms serving that area up to today's rules; on projects under $209,208 (the 2026 figure) that duty is limited.
      • Fire safety: building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
      • How many stalls: Sacramento uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
      • California extras: California asks more of a stall than the federal rules. In a large restroom, 5% of the stalls must be wheelchair accessible, not just one. The accessible stall needs more open floor in front of the toilet, so it's deeper, and the aisle outside its door must be 48 inches wide, against 42. Stall doors need a privacy latch, and every restroom door carries California's circle or triangle symbol. Give your layout to your architect before you order.
      • Single-user and all-gender restrooms: a one-person restroom must be signed as all-gender. A shared all-gender room is allowed in place of separate men's and women's rooms if every toilet is in a floor-to-ceiling privacy compartment whose door locks from the inside and shows when it's occupied.
      • Permits: Sacramento requires a permit for remodeling and follows California's list of work that needs none. Its exempt list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work", and the state list adds movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. Neither names toilet partitions, so ask the Building Division's public counter (916-808-5318) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.

      Rules change, so confirm your project with the City of Sacramento Building Division or your architect. The accessible stall's sizes are in our ADA compliance guide, and fixture spacing is in the restroom layout guide.

      How many stalls a Sacramento restroom needs

      Sacramento counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.

      These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.

      To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Sacramento Building Division sets the final number.

      Installation in Sacramento

      Next Partitions supplies the partitions; a contractor you hire installs them. Every order comes with shop drawings: a plan of your room with every panel, door and pilaster sized, which the installer sets out from.

      Need an installer? Our directory of partition installers in Sacramento lists local installers. Ask for installation in your quote request and we collect their prices for your job.

      In Sacramento, contractors pay the city's business operations tax when a building permit is issued, and permits go to the owner, the owner's agent or a licensed contractor. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.

      Our installation guide shows the work step by step, and how to measure for toilet partitions covers what to send for an accurate quote.

      What installation labor and sales tax add in Sacramento

      • Local labor rates: carpenters in the Sacramento–Roseville–Folsom area earn a median of $35.79 an hour, about 23% above the national median of $29.12. It's a guide to local labor rates, not a quote: installers set their own prices.
      • Public jobs: California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Sacramento County that is $68.58 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
      • Sales tax: 8.75% in Sacramento: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation authority and 1% city.
      • Tax on installation: in California, installation labor billed separately isn't taxed.
      • Buying without installation: partitions shipped to Sacramento are taxable. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.

      How tax applies depends on your contract, so confirm with your accountant or the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration.

      What Sacramento buyers order partitions for

      • Schools: HDPE or phenolic, heights by age group, vandal-resistant hardware.
      • Restaurants and bars: a finish that matches the dining room, in a material that survives the nightly clean.
      • Offices and tenant build-outs: overhead braced stalls that work with any ceiling.
      • Warehouses, plants and distribution centers: stalls that take hard use and washdown.
      • Churches, gyms and clinics: privacy options and accessible stalls sized to the 2010 ADA Standards.
      • Government offices and public buildings: stainless steel or phenolic that stands up to heavy daily use.

      Delivery to Sacramento and nearby cities

      Toilet partitions for Sacramento ship by freight carrier, crated, palletized and tracked, and freight is quoted with the partitions. Delivery is curbside, with a liftgate on request if the site has no loading dock, so give the delivery address and say whether it has a dock in your quote request.

      We also deliver to Elk Grove, Roseville, Citrus Heights, Folsom, Rancho Cordova, Rocklin, Davis and Woodland, and every other ZIP code in the Sacramento area. We ship to all 50 states: see the full service area.

      Frequently Asked Questions

      Do I need a permit to replace toilet partitions in Sacramento?

      Sacramento requires a permit for remodeling and follows California's list of work that needs none. Its exempt list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work", and the state list adds movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. Neither names toilet partitions, so ask the Building Division's public counter (916-808-5318) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.

      How many stalls does a Sacramento restroom need?

      For a building that holds 100 people, an office needs at least 3 women's stalls, 1 men's stall and 1 urinal, a restaurant needs at least 2 women's stalls, 1 men's stall and 1 urinal and a school needs at least 2 women's stalls, 1 men's stall and 1 urinal. The table above covers other sizes. Confirm the number for your building with the City of Sacramento Building Division.

      Who can install toilet partitions in Sacramento?

      A contractor you hire. We supply the partitions and the shop drawings. In Sacramento the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more. Our directory lists partition installers in Sacramento, and you can ask for installation prices with your quote.

      Which partition material is best in Sacramento?

      The dry climate suits all five. Choose HDPE or phenolic only where the room itself gets wet: pools, locker rooms and restrooms that are hosed down.

      What tax applies to partitions delivered to Sacramento?

      8.75% in Sacramento: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation authority and 1% city. Partitions shipped to Sacramento are taxable. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
